notes: The supplied instrumental 'with' was given to τόν, the article of the accusative πηλόν, on the ground that it follows the case-preposition pattern. Rule 21 forbids that in terms — it speaks throughout of a preposition realizing the governed word's own case — and rule 106's accusative arm gives the answer: an accusative has no case for an English preposition to realize, so a preposition standing over an accusative object is the verb's own phrasal government and stays inside the verb's unit, the governed word keeping a bare noun.
